answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by requiring each new identity to burn a non-refundable fee and then earn trust slowly: full rewards unlock only after a continuous thread of peer-attested work across many epochs. Like pigment in ink, the burn marks the identity permanently, and there is no harbor for shortcuts - splitting into 1,000 fakes means paying the burn 1,000 times and redoing months of work for each, costing far more than honest participation pays.
